lessons.title: Negotiating an Offer: Tax-Efficient Asks Beyond the Headline CTC

children.text: Aakash, a data scientist in Bengaluru, is negotiating a move from a ₹22 lakh job. The new company offers ₹26 lakh CTC. He asks for ₹28 lakh. The recruiter says the band is capped at ₹26 lakh, "but we are flexible on everything else."

Most candidates hear that as a polite no. It is actually an invitation. Without adding a rupee to CTC, Aakash can restructure the offer to save ₹69,630 of tax a year, which is worth about as much as a ₹94,000 raise. This lesson shows you how to negotiate the structure once the headline number stops moving.

body.text: When the CTC is fixed, negotiate what the CTC is made of.

children.text: Step 1: Compare offers on what you keep, not on CTC
Before negotiating, rebuild every offer on the same basis. Everything from Chapters 1 to 3 goes into one question: how much will I actually keep, and how much of it is guaranteed?
Guaranteed cash after tax
: fixed salary minus employee PF, professional tax and tax
Expected variable after tax
: target bonus × realistic payout rate, minus tax
Retirement money
: employer PF and NPS, valued fully only if you will not need it soon
Tax-free benefits you would pay for anyway
: meals, phone, laptop, insurance
Gratuity
: count it only if you expect to stay 5 years
Step 2: The asks that cost the employer nothing extra

body.title: Pick the better ask
body.question: Aakash is choosing between two relocation packages from Mumbai to Bengaluru, both costing the employer about ₹1,20,000. Which is more tax-efficient for him?
options: A ₹1,20,000 relocation allowance paid in his first salary
The company directly pays movers, his flight and 12 days of hotel stay on transfer
All three are taxed the same
body.explanation: Costs of the transfer itself paid directly, such as travel and moving, and hotel accommodation for up to 15 days on transfer are generally not taxable. A lump-sum relocation allowance or joining bonus of the same amount is fully taxable salary.

children.text: Aakash restructures his ₹26 lakh

Aakash will stay in the new regime. The default offer has basic of ₹13,00,000 (50%), HRA ₹6,50,000, employer PF ₹1,56,000, gratuity ₹62,500 and special allowance ₹4,31,500. He asks HR to move ₹2,67,800 of special allowance into employer NPS at 14% of basic, a meal card, phone reimbursement and gift vouchers.

columns.label: Default offer
points: No employer NPS, no flexi components

children.text: Gross salary in both cases: ₹26,00,000 minus employer PF ₹1,56,000 minus gratuity ₹62,500 = ₹23,81,500
Restructured: also less employer NPS ₹1,82,000 and flexi ₹85,800 = ₹20,38,700. Slab tax = ₹2,00,000 + 25% of ₹38,700 (₹9,675) = ₹2,09,675. With cess: ₹2,18,060
Tax saved: ₹69,630 a year

stats.label: Equivalent raise
stats.context: Extra taxable salary needed to keep the same amount

body.text: Tax saved is not the same as cash in hand. Aakash's wealth rises by ₹69,630, but his spendable cash falls by ₹1,12,370 because NPS is locked. If he needs liquidity, a smaller NPS share with the full flexi basket still saves a meaningful amount.

children.text: Joining bonuses: taxable, but timing is negotiable
A joining bonus is fully taxed as salary in the tax year it is paid. That makes the payment date a negotiation lever, especially when you change jobs near the end of a tax year.

Priya joins a new employer on 1 March 2027 with a ₹3,00,000 joining bonus. In tax year 2026-27, her taxable income from her old job and one month at the new job is ₹10,50,000. In tax year 2027-28, her taxable income from her new salary will be ₹20,00,000 before any bonus. Assume slabs stay the same.

body.title: Tax on Priya's ₹3,00,000 joining bonus by payment timing

children.text: All in March
: taxable income rises from ₹10,50,000 to ₹13,50,000, losing the rebate. Tax ₹85,800
All in April
: taxed in 2027-28 on top of ₹20,00,000, mostly at 25% plus cess. Extra tax ₹78,000
Split
: ₹1,50,000 in March takes 2026-27 exactly to ₹12,00,000, so tax stays nil. ₹1,50,000 in April costs ₹39,000. Total ₹39,000

body.title: Priya's saving from splitting
body.prompt: How much tax does Priya save by splitting her joining bonus across the two tax years, compared with taking it all in March 2027?

body.text: Read the clawback clause. If you must repay a joining bonus in a later tax year, tax already paid on it is not straightforwardly recovered, and deduction of the repayment is a contested area. Negotiate a shorter clawback period or a pro-rata repayment rather than relying on getting the tax back.

children.text: Notice period buyouts: ask for a gross-up

If your new employer reimburses the notice period buyout you pay your old employer, that reimbursement is taxable salary for you. The buyout you pay is not deductible. So a "we will reimburse your ₹1,20,000 buyout" promise leaves you out of pocket by the tax on it.

body.caption: The amount your new employer should pay so that you keep the full buyout after tax.

body.title: Gross up the buyout
body.prompt: Aakash has to pay a ₹1,20,000 notice period buyout. His marginal rate including cess is 31.2%. What reimbursement should he ask for so that he is left with exactly ₹1,20,000 after tax?

body.title: The relocation hotel rule
body.textWithBlank: Hotel accommodation provided by the employer on transfer is not a taxable perquisite for a stay of up to ___ days.
body.explanation: Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 excludes hotel accommodation of up to 15 days on transfer. Beyond that, it is valued at the lower of actual charges and 24% of salary for the period.

children.text: Putting it into words

body.title: Aakash writes back to HR
body.scenario: The recruiter has confirmed ₹26 lakh CTC is final. Aakash wants to accept, but with the restructuring from this lesson, relocation paid as actual costs, a reimbursed ₹1,20,000 notice buyout, and his parents added to group health cover. He is worried about sounding difficult.
body.prompt: Draft the key points of Aakash's reply. What should he ask for, in what order, and how should he frame it?
body.modelAnswer: Frame it as accepting the number and asking only for structure: "I am happy to go ahead at ₹26 lakh CTC. To make the move work, could we look at the components within that CTC?" Then list specific, low-cost asks. (1) Within CTC: employer NPS at 14% of basic, meal card of ₹4,400 a month, phone reimbursement and gift vouchers, with the balance in special allowance. This costs the employer nothing extra. (2) Relocation: movers, flights and up to 15 days of hotel stay paid directly on actuals rather than as a cash allowance. (3) Notice buyout: reimbursement grossed up to about ₹1,74,400, or alternatively a joining bonus of that amount, with any clawback pro-rated. (4) Benefits: parents added to the group health policy, even if he pays a small top-up premium. Keep it to one short email, give reasons in a line each, and make it easy for HR to say yes to most of it. Structure asks are routinely granted because they are budget-neutral.

body.title: Before you sign: tax-efficient negotiation checklist
steps: Rebuild every offer on guaranteed cash after tax, expected variable, and retirement money
Ask for employer NPS and flexi components within the same CTC
Ask for laptops, phones and relocation to be provided or paid on actuals, not as cash allowances
Time any joining bonus to the tax year where your marginal rate is lower, or split it
Ask for a grossed-up notice buyout reimbursement
Negotiate pro-rata clawbacks on joining and retention bonuses
Check PF basis, variable payout history and group health cover before accepting

body.text: Figures use tax year 2026-27 rules for resident individuals, and assume the same slabs in 2027-28 for illustration. Employer policies and tax treatment of specific arrangements vary. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax, legal or career advice.

points: When CTC is capped, negotiate its structure: employer NPS, flexi components, and benefits paid in kind.
Aakash saved ₹69,630 a year at the same ₹26 lakh CTC, about the value of a ₹94,000 raise, though with less spendable cash.
Company-provided laptops, relocation on actual costs and up to 15 days of transfer hotel stay beat equivalent cash allowances.
Joining bonuses are taxed when paid. Splitting Priya's bonus across two tax years saved ₹46,800.
Reimbursed notice buyouts are taxable, so ask for a gross-up: buyout ÷ (1 − your marginal rate).
Read clawback clauses carefully. Tax on a repaid bonus is hard to recover.
